props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the control and withholds it from submission.

props.name: error
props.description: The validation message. Its presence drives `aria-invalid`.

props.name: format
props.description: A template for `aria-valuetext`, where `$v` is the value and `$m` is the maximum — "$v of $m". What a screen reader announces instead of a bare number.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the field invalid independently of whether `error` is set.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name, and the label rendered above the control.

props.name: name
props.description: Native form semantics. The control is named by the host attribute.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Renders the numeric output beside the label.  Off by default: a value the consumer is already displaying in their own UI should not be duplicated here, and a bare number with no unit is often worse than none.

props.name: step
props.description: Granularity. `0` means any value the browser can represent.

ai.summary: Picks one number from a range, on a track the reader drags or arrows across.
whenToUse: The value is a number on a known range, such as volume or a budget ceiling
The exact number matters less than where it sits in the range
Steps are meaningful — volume in fives, budget in tens
whenNotToUse: The reader must type an exact figure — use an Input with type=number
There are fewer than five discrete choices — use a Radio Group
You need two ends of a range — use two sliders, or a dedicated range control
ai.accessibility: A real `<input type="range">`, so the platform owns the slider role, `aria-valuenow`, the arrow/Page/Home/End model, and the touch target — all of which a `<div role="slider">` reimplementation tends to lose. `aria-valuetext` takes a consumer-supplied `format` template ("$v of $m"), because §6 says locale is consumer-supplied. The label points at the control by id; the description and error ids are appended together rather than one replacing the other.
ai.example: <sk-slider name="volume" label="Volume" value="40" show-value format="$v of $m"></sk-slider>
knownLimitations: The thumb's square shape is asserted on Chromium and Firefox; WebKit exposes neither thumb pseudo-element to getComputedStyle
SSR consumers must pass an explicit id — the counter differs between server and client
The visual fill on Chromium comes from the platform's own rendering, not a custom element
